segments.text: You own two stocks. One's up, one's down. Watch which one you sell, because it's the exact wrong one.
You sell the winner to lock in the gain. And you hold the loser, waiting for it to come back.
Why? A loss hurts about twice as much as the same gain feels good. So you'll do almost anything to avoid feeling it.
But the math says the opposite. This one habit quietly wrecks more portfolios than any bad tip.
That's loss aversion. Honest verdict on the channel.
